mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in at least 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in at least 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 3% indicates supply-side constraints with inflationary pressure, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.25 (i.e., >3% annualized)
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the 90th percentile of the past five years, coupled with a simultaneous decline in personal income growth (PAYEMS), signals a precautionary savings regime that reduces consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 90th percentile of last 5 years AND PAYEMS monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 0.5% for six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals an accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% for six consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL annualized < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 300k per month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 300000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of triggered events.
